scenes.title: A bell every four beats
scenes.narration: Imagine a bell ringing on every fourth beat. It rings at four, eight and twelve. Beat seven sits one step before eight. Adding one to seven lands on a bell. Keep that one-step move in your pocket.

scenes.title: When two bells ring
scenes.narration: A second bell rings on every sixth beat. Both bells start at zero. Which beat after twenty comes first just one step before both bells ring together?

scenes.title: Look for the shared beat
scenes.narration: The four-beat bell rings at four, eight and twelve. The six-beat bell rings at six and twelve. The two meet every twelve beats. After twenty, their next shared beat is twenty-four. Step back to twenty-three. Its remainders are three when divided by four and five when divided by six.

scenes.title: Two beats early
scenes.narration: Change the bells to six and ten beats. Count the beats from fifty to one hundred and twenty-five, including both ends, that come two beats before a simultaneous ring. How could you find all of them without testing every beat?

scenes.title: Move the interval too
scenes.narration: Add two to both ends of the interval. The shared rings must lie between fifty-two and one hundred and twenty-seven. Six and ten first meet at thirty, then repeat every thirty beats. Sixty, ninety and one hundred and twenty are the only multiples of thirty inside the shifted interval.

scenes.title: Return to the question
scenes.narration: Now step back two beats from each ring. Fifty-eight, eighty-eight and one hundred and eighteen all work. There are three beats. If the question asks for the beat before a ring, return to the original scale before answering.
